sentences.text: Shri Vishal Patidar, learned counsel for the applicant  Shri Rahul Solanki, learned Govt.Advocate for the resp  ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is first application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail to the applicant, in connection with FIR/Crime No.506/2024, Date:-(Not mentioned) registered at P.S. - Raoti, District - Ratlam (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 376, 506 of the IPC.
2. Prosecution story in brief is that, prior to the incident the prosecutrix and the applicant were known to each other.
On 23.4.2023 the prosecutrix was returning to home alongwith applicant by motorcycle, the applicant forcibly took the prosecutrix to his house and committed rape upon her.
He threatened the prosecutrix that if she will narrate the incident to someone, he will kill her.
The matter was reported on 30.9.2024 by the prosecutrix.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that the prosecutrix is major and married lady.

There was physical relationship between both of them, therefore, she was consenting party for sexual intercourse, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:31974 2 MCRC-46180-2024 but due to some dispute, the prosecutrix lodged a false FIR belatedly for more than one year and five months without any plausible explanation.
The applicant is in custody since 3.10.2024.
The conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time for its disposal.

Under these circumstances,
prayer is made for grant of bail to the applicant.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection.

5. Having considered the submissions advanced from counsel for the parties and also considering the facts and circumstances and custody period of the applicant, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant - Bahadur be released on bail upon his/her furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his/her appearance before the trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the trial Court during pendency of the trial.
It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
7. M.Cr.C. stands disposed off, accordingly.
C.c. as per rules.
